// delete a user account and all history: comments, posts and votes
 public static bool DeleteUser(string userName)
 {
 using (var db = new whoaverseEntities())
 {
 using (var tmpUserManager = new UserManager<WhoaVerseUser>(new UserStore<WhoaVerseUser>(new ApplicationDbContext())))
 {
 var tmpuser = tmpUserManager.FindByName(userName);
 if (tmpuser != null)
 {
 // remove voting history for submisions
 db.Votingtrackers.RemoveRange(db.Votingtrackers.Where(x => x.UserName == userName));

 // remove voting history for comments
 db.Commentvotingtrackers.RemoveRange(db.Commentvotingtrackers.Where(x => x.UserName == userName));

 // remove all comments
 var comments = db.Comments.Where(c => c.Name == userName).ToList();
 foreach (Comment c in comments)
 {
 c.Name = "deleted";
 c.CommentContent = "deleted by user";
 }
 db.SaveChanges();

 // remove all submissions
 var submissions = db.Messages.Where(c => c.Name == userName).ToList();
 foreach (Message s in submissions)
 {
 if (s.Type == 1)
 {
 s.Name = "deleted";
 s.MessageContent = "deleted by user";
 s.Title = "deleted by user";
 }
 else
 {
 s.Name = "deleted";
 s.Linkdescription = "deleted by user";
 s.MessageContent = "http://voat.co";
 }
 }

 // resign from all moderating positions
 db.SubverseAdmins.RemoveRange(db.SubverseAdmins.Where(m => m.Username.Equals(userName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)));

 // delete comment reply notifications
 db.Commentreplynotifications.RemoveRange(db.Commentreplynotifications.Where(crp => crp.Recipient.Equals(userName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)));

 // delete post reply notifications
 db.Postreplynotifications.RemoveRange(db.Postreplynotifications.Where(prp => prp.Recipient.Equals(userName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)));

 // delete private messages
 db.Privatemessages.RemoveRange(db.Privatemessages.Where(pm => pm.Recipient.Equals(userName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)));

 // TODO:
 // keep this updated as new features are added (delete sets etc)

 // username will stay permanently reserved

 db.SaveChanges();

 return true;
 }
 // user account could not be found
 return false;
 }

 }
 }

Summary of the Previous CHALLENGE

Oh wow guys that challenge took off! I'm really appreciative of all who contributed, and proud of those who said you couldn't, but did anyway. We had a lot of new great content in world creating, and some very interesting new ways to present it. I haven't gone through all of them with reviews yet (They're still being posted!), but great work everyone. Another big thanks goes to those who contributed in editing, feedback, and suggestions both in the post and in the IRC writer's Lounge.

I want you all to hold onto your worlds you've created. there may be an additional CHALLENGE coming up referring back to them, since everyone was so excited (gr33narrow winks and says "hint hint"). If you haven't contributed and still want to, it's not too late! Just go here.

One update I'll be making is the fact there won't be rules, but "Guidelines." They're the same but the rules kind of scared some people, so Guidelines is a less abrasive term.

One thing that we ran into issues with was the character limit. It would say "wait 30 seconds" and then you would, then submit with the same error "wait 30 seconds" and finally give up and break your story in half. Then the glorious TRIPLE POSTS started. Mass confusions happened. The POTUS even called wondering what the eff was up. Here's how we can avoid that in the future if you have a long post:

  1. Type your story in word, google docs, whatever.
  2. Post the first half at the comment to the Post with PART 1 at the start and (Continued below) at the end.
  3. Post your second half as a reply to your initial comment with PART 2. BUT WAIT THERE'S MORE
  4. If you have a third, fourth, or even fifth, go ahead and reply to your PART 1 comment and label it 3,4 and so on.

Those guidelines SHOULD help out with 1) no more triple posts. and 2) not get lost in the comments thread.

Deep in a crowded, steamy and wet jungle we find ourselves skipping across its canopy at breakneck speed. Green scruffy rain forest and jungle tree tops stretch for as far as the eye can see dipping over the horizon. A Small clearing comes into view, a doorway of corrugated steel sheets rusty with the touch of time, and the telltale dampness of the heat in which it sits. We move in closer to take inspect.

Consisting of a heavily reinforced steel bar and a small hatch at the top the doors rusty caustic brown blends into the forest floor. Beside the door the small shack hides in the shadow of the canopy and reaches a short way back with the forest carved away to make space. Beside it sits a seemingly very large water tower, showing the same signature signs of a life in the jungle rusty and kissed by father time himself. Small markings of what used to be on the side are just ledgible “ EA R E “. is all that can be made from it but a thick hose leads to the shacks roof. Lets check inside shall we?

Creaking in the damp, nearly stuck in its frame the door hardly gives way and finally opens with a thud. Amazingly it wasn't even locked. Inside we find a row of 8 lockers lining the wall to the left, two doors to the right one plain like an office door, and one looks to be a lavatory door. The far end of the room is a coat rack. Behind the office door all that is found is two standard laundry dryers plugged in and functioning. Odd, there didnt seem to be any power, following the cords from them up to the ceiling of the room and over into the lavatory it seems. Wonder what thats all about?

As we approach the door to the lavatory we find it has steam in the window, and the rushing sound of water hits our ears followed by a murmur in the room. Peculiar. Slowly we open the door the steam hitting our faces hot and a smell of, its hard to describe. It smells like that first rain in a hot summer. So as we head inside we see where the wires go. A large battery bank lie against one wall, while a shower stall lie on the other with the cords coming over the wall and dangling lazily to their connection. From inside the shower a quiet voice comes over the thunder of the water quiet as a whisper.

“piikaa.” it says when suddenly the sound of a starship landing is heard, shaking the ground around us with its weight and volume. We rush outside to see the nimbus 3000 piloted by zap brannigan, who exits the ship immidatly followed by the green arrow brandishing her bow at us. Lastly a samauri steps forth and greets us

“greetings, you may call me Sento-Senpai, we are here for the electric one.” he states, almost an order, while the captain slurps deeply on his banana milkshake.

“enough bibble babble green whatever, go get it.” he chimes with a sneer, tossing the empty cup at the samurai.

“you're useless, you know that?” she scolds as she stoms into the small shack.

“who are you then? Some sort of, uh. Say what are you?” we get asked by the great captain his holiness zap brannigan.

“oh, we were just uh, well we own this land. You see?” we say as the green arrow comes back holding pikachu soaking wet, still covered in bubbly suds flopping to the ground with a splat as they drip from his tail.

“Yan we go now?” she queries.

“Yes, great archer. Let us embark.” says the samurai stiffly.

“Off we are then, you folks take care now. Enjoy the ehh, goodbye.” says zap, as he turns on his heel and makes his way back into his ship, only to take off shortly after.

Now here we are, left dazed, confused and befuddled by the events that took place before us. Left with some shack built by god knows who. Any one able to tell us? We are greatly confused.
